- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to over-forecast (especially after spikes), so reduce forecast peak values by 5–15%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply a “cool-down” rule: cap forecast at 1–2 standard deviations above recent mean for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive, model often overreacts — suppress early forecast increases by 10–20% until sentiment stabilizes.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon — if forecast is >1.5σ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 10–15%.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model tends to over-forecast — apply a “sentiment dampener”: reduce forecast by 5–10% if sentiment variance is low.
- If true outcome is below forecast for 3+ consecutive days, model is likely overconfident — reduce next forecast by 5–10% unless confirmed by new event data.
